#1604. Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

“Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

“I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “But this was a top-class performance.”

It has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

The home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO

Leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

“That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

[It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

It’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

[Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

Exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No

For each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

Energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

We have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

[Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

The ref told me at half-time that they’ve taken it off me. I didn’t know he [Bogle] was there to be fair. I just got up and went ‘Bang!’ It is what it is. I’ll take the assist!

I didn’t know anything about it [being given credit for the second goal]. I said to the ref, I don’t fancy telling him [Calvert-Lewin]. To be fair he’s still raging. He’s raging with the goal but happy with the result.

It’s about having an understanding with the players around you. With Dom up there, you know he’s going to win everything so you have to get the runners around him.

It’s about the rotation like today. When James Justin goes wider there’s space inside. Dom occupies two centre-backs so there’s always pockets.

Regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

A proper stuffing for Newcastle as Leeds continue to impress and climb up to third.

It’s never a problem to come to Elland Road and the singing of Marching On Together before kick-off makes this one of the top three atmospheres in the country, easily. There are problems with VAR, though, and the whole stadium has just seen the ball strike Matias Fernanzes-Pardo’s hand in the area. Leeds kick off, attacking the South Stand, from left to right, as they always prefer to do. Justin and Bogle combine on the right and Bogle bends a pass inside HAll to Stach who chooses to cross rather than shoot. It hits Botman and goes out for a corner.

Leeds are in their home kit of white with yellow and blue pinstripe hoops, Newcastle in their navy away kit.

Anthony [Elanga] is injured. Unfortunately we have to investigate further how long he will be out but obviously we miss him. We wish him to come back as quickly as possible. It could be [a long-term injury] but he will get another MRI next week and then we’ll see.

Lewis Hall is the perfect player profile for how we play. he is a young lad still and we are very excited [that he has signed a new contract].

The start was not easy. We didn’t have lots of time to prepare for pre-season and that’s one reason we are happy and satisfied with the start. But there is potential and we will work hard on the margins we want to improve.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

But Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

Jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

There are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

This is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

He formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the new boy Fernandez-Pardo?

Mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. And yet he was always gracious about Leeds and particularly fond of Don Revie. He was one of very few football people without a strong Leeds United connection who went to his funeral in 1989.

Apparently he was injured in training, the nature of the injury is unspecified.

Newcastle have made a very good start particularly in their transitional moments on the counter-attack. We have to be switched on today to get the next points.

After many years of suffering our supporters deserve it [high expectations]. It’s good but we are far away from not being humble. Our feet are on the ground. We know the second year is always difficult. We have made a good start and it is always important to ride the momentum as long as possible.

Eddie Howe has left a legacy and the culture he created is still around. Matthias has to work with it. They are unbeaten. they are very dangerous with many pacy players up front. It’s important not to lose the ball too easily and always be switched on against Newcastle.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

The architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. His two goals that night were his sixth and seventh against Leeds in eight matches for Leicester and the Toon. Back in the last century and at the turn of this one, Alan Shearer scored 21 league goals in 23 games against Leeds for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle, it can feel like one bogeyman passing the baton to another.

Newcastle’s sound form with their new model team this season has been based on searing pace and their ability on the counter whether with runners, in the case of Anthony Elanga, or with long diagonals against Tottenham that ripped a hole in the left side of their defence. Leeds rallied from being overrun by Brentford at half-time in their last home game to switch from three at the back to four and wrest back the initiative and while they reverted for the Brighton draw, in both games it was the introduction of Ao Tanaka in midfield that gave them control.

It is genuinely hard to decide whether the 6-3 defeat by Chelsea in the Carabao Cup from being 2-0 up at Stamford Bridge is significant to Leeds league form. One simplistic way of looking at it would be to say Leeds reserves were better than Chelsea’s reserves in the first half and Chelsea’s first-team were better than Leeds reserves and their shaky, debutant keeper in the second. But any similar defensive frailties tonight and there will be jitters over the next week before the international break. Newcastle, by contrast, toiled in their 1-0 victory over Millwall but the result glosses over a lack of incision for long spells of it.

Joe Rodon is out for Leeds for at least another month while Newcastle have changed to withholding information about their treatment room under Matthias Jaissle who says that it should be ‘confidential’. We do know that Joelinton, William Osula and Dan Burn are likely to still be out given the nature of their injuries but Amar Dedic, who came off at half-time at the New Den with a thigh or hamstring problem, may be back.

#1603. Chelsea Transfer News: Alonso Tells Right-Back To Leave

Chelsea transfer news: Xabi Alonso has reportedly told Malo Gusto to find a new club, according to CaughtOffside, who are citing Simon Phillips’ Substack. The report claims the 23-year-old France international does not suit the wing-back system Alonso has built at Stamford Bridge. It also floats a surprise swap that would send Gusto to Liverpool and reunite Alonso with Jeremie Frimpong, his former Bayer Leverkusen right wing-back.

Liverpool’s interest has history. They tried to sign Gusto on loan on deadline day, but Chelsea refused anything short of a permanent deal. Their right-back problem has run since Trent Alexander-Arnold left. Frimpong cost around £29.5million and has battled injuries and form, while Ronald Araujo is a centre-back covering on a season-long loan from Barcelona.

Gusto’s standing has slipped quickly. He started three of the first four league games, yet Josh Acheampong has since taken his place, and reports say he will be fourth choice behind Acheampong, Marco Palestra and Reece James once James returns from injury in early 2027.

His strength is defending, with 73 tackles and 36 chances created in 45 appearances last season. The weakness is end product, because three goals and five assists are modest for a wing-back who must supply Alonso’s right-hand width.

Frimpong supplies exactly that. The 25-year-old Dutchman scored 28 of his 30 Leverkusen goals under Alonso and thrives on pace and early crosses. Defending is his flaw, at 5ft 8in and with a poor injury record at Anfield.

No. Chelsea are fifth with 16 points from 10 games, but they have lost four, including 1-0 at Sunderland last Sunday and 3-0 at Brentford, and they concede too easily. Frimpong would add another attacker to a right side that already has James, Acheampong, Palestra and Pedro Neto, and he does nothing for a shaky back line. With no European football this season, Chelsea don’t need that many right-sided options anyway.

The money matters too. Both players have contracts until 2030 and similar valuations, so a straight swap brings Chelsea no cash and leaves Liverpool with their problem solved.

Sell Gusto instead, preferably abroad, since Paris Saint-Germain have been linked and Chelsea are reportedly open to cutting their asking price. Then spend that fee on a defensive midfielder or centre-back, because that is where Alonso’s team needs help.

Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all contacted Bournemouth about England midfielder Alex Scott, according to CaughtOffside, which cites The i Paper. #1599. Liverpool Transfer News: Dutch Star’s Agent Tests Market

Liverpool transfer news: Ryan Gravenberch’s agent, José Fortes Rodriguez, is exploring ways to take his client out of Anfield, according to CaughtOffside. The site relays a claim from the X account @ITKSpace that Fortes has held “loose but direct contact” with several European clubs, none of them named. No formal exit request has been lodged, and the 24-year-old could still stay, so this reads like a camp checking the market rather than a player pushing to leave.

Liverpool hold the stronger hand. His six-year extension, signed in March, runs to 2032, so any buyer would face a substantial asking price. Real Madrid have been linked before, though nothing here says they are interested now.

Iraola’s 4-2-3-1 relies on two central midfielders, and Gravenberch, so commanding at the base of Arne Slot’s title-winning side, has struggled to settle. Iraola benched him for three straight games at one stage, he collected a second yellow card in the 3-0 home defeat by Manchester City on 11 October, and a heel problem has since kept him out of the Arsenal and Fenerbahçe games. He has no goals and one assist in the league this term.

His strengths are clear. At 6ft 3in he carries the ball through pressure and starts attacks from deep. Defending space and tracking runners is the weakness, and it shows when his partner also surges forward.

No, not this winter and not at a price set by his worst few weeks. Gravenberch is 24, tied down until 2032, and his market value has slipped sharply since last December, so selling now would hand a buyer the bargain that March contract was meant to rule out.

The real problem sits elsewhere. Iraola received no new midfielder in the summer, and his double pivot has no natural holding player. Gravenberch has admitted he prefers the number eight role, yet Mac Allister and Szoboszlai, who started the 3-1 win at Crystal Palace that lifted Liverpool to fourth, already occupy those spots. Nineteen-year-old Trey Nyoni has mostly played the deeper role this season.

Keep him through January, get him fit, and judge him again in a settled pairing. If Liverpool then sign a proper holding midfielder next summer, Gravenberch becomes a surplus eight, and a big-club bid at the right figure would deserve a hearing. Selling before that signing arrives just removes the one midfielder who can still carry the ball out of pressure.

#1598. Villa Midfielder Has £80m Price Tag For Arsenal: Is He Worth It?

Arsenal transfer news: Aston Villa do not regard Boubacar Kamara as available, even with Arsenal interested, according to CaughtOffside. The report says an offer of around £80m could change that stance, although Villa negotiate from strength because the 26-year-old’s contract runs until 2030.

January looks highly unlikely. Villa have already lost Amadou Onana to a torn ACL suffered at the World Cup, and the Belgian is not expected back until around April. Unai Emery cannot lose a second holding midfielder in the middle of a season. The summer is different. CaughtOffside says Villa could entertain a significant bid then, provided they can reinvest the money in a proper replacement and strengthen the squad around him.

TBR Football reported in July 2025 that he sat on Arsenal’s long list of midfield targets, and his numbers explain why. Kamara has started all 10 of his Premier League games this season, completing 86.3% of his passes, including 83 line-breaking balls, while making 28 tackles and 40 recoveries. He wins 56% of his duels and can play at centre-back, which would give Mikel Arteta cover in two positions.

The weaknesses are just as clear. He has no goals this season, only three shots and an xG of 0.14, and he has committed 20 fouls and conceded a penalty. He also missed the closing weeks of 2024/25 through injury.

The role he would play is obvious: a ball-playing six next to Declan Rice. Martín Zubimendi occupies it now, and Arsenal lead the league with 27 points from 10 games, six clear of Manchester City, with seven clean sheets.

No, not at that price. Arsenal spent £75m on Bruno Guimarães in August, and Arteta still has Rice, Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Martin Ødegaard and Myles Lewis-Skelly competing for the same central spaces.

Villa’s insistence on reinvesting the fee also hands them the leverage, which means Arsenal would pay a premium on a seller’s timetable.

The only sensible trigger is a departure, perhaps Zubimendi or the 30-year-old Merino, leaving Arsenal short of a proven Premier League six. Kamara is a better holding midfielder than most of the market, but a title-leading side already has that job covered, and £80m would buy cover rather than improvement.

Published: 17:01 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:58 EST, 13 November 2026

Kevin De Bruyne's wife Michelle has opened up on her family's struggles in Naples and desire to move back home to Belgium one day.

De Bruyne, 35, joined Napoli in the summer of 2025 after leaving Manchester City following a legendary ten-year spell.

But things haven't gone to plan in Italy, with De Bruyne struggling for fitness in his first season, while he also clashed with former boss Antonio Conte.

The situation hasn't improved much this time around under Max Allegri as Napoli currently sit 10th in Serie A, and reports broke earlier this season that the Belgian midfielder was involved in a dressing room bust-up with team-mates.

And De Bruyne's wife Michele, who he married in 2017, reflected on the turbulence in an interview with Belgian magazine NINA back in September.

'Of course, we think about the future together,' he said. 'And increasingly often, we say to each other: "We are going to live here in Limburg. The sooner we get here, the better".'

Kevin De Bruyne's wife Michelle has opened up on her family's struggles living in Naples

De Bruyne moved to Napoli in the summer of 2025 after a glittering 10 years at Manchester City

Limburg is a province in Belgium, and although Michelle insisted that she thought Naples was a beautiful place to live with great weather and food, she spoke about the toll that life in Italy has had on her partner and their three children, Mason, Rome and Suri.

'Kevin leads a very restricted life in Napoli,' she added. 'It's not much fun for him. Besides, we can't do anything together as a family in the city. That's the other side of the coin, isn't it?

She later added: 'At a certain point, football is no longer the priority. You have achieved everything, done everything. Why would you then turn your children’s lives upside down?'

De Bruyne, who is one of the highest paid players in Italy, signed a two-year contract when he arrived at Napoli but it wasn't certain that he would make it into the second part of that deal in the summer.

Reflecting on his first year ahead of the World Cup, De Bruyne insisted he was 'happy' that Conte had departed.

'Obviously it was difficult for me because Conte has a very different vision of football to mine,' De Bruyne said.

'In truth, I never had the opportunity to play in my preferred position. In any case, I always tried to give my all for the team. We played very defensively. If you try to win every game by a one-goal margin with a 4-5-1 formation, you play a certain type of football.

De Bruyne signed a two-year deal at Napoli and is unlikely to extend his time in Italy

'At the start of the season, we sat back even deeper. Our centre-forward scored just 10 goals, so you know the statistics are not going to be great…'

He later added: 'For me, yes (I'm happy Conte has gone). As far as I am concerned, he was not obliged to stay. There were promises made last summer on the way that we would be playing, but at the end of the day not much of it happened.

'I found that a pity. Football needs to be enjoyable, and unfortunately, I found that aspect lacking.

'There’s no point beating around the bush, we have different visions of football. I never got to play in my position under Conte.'

#1596. Max Dowman breaks Jude Bellingham record: what makes the Arsenal gem so special?

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 11:31

Max Dowman, who turns 17 soon, has already made history in the Premier League, the Champions League and for England

It seems that every piece of news about Max Dowman starts the same way: the young Arsenal player has broken another record. At 16, the Englishman has already been the youngest player to score in the Premier League, to play in the Champions League and to win the English league title.

This week, he added two more marks to the list: he became the youngest player to represent the England Under-21s and, three days later, the youngest to score for the side, surpassing records that belonged to Jude Bellingham.

The question is not only how many more records he can break, but what makes Dowman such a special talent and how far his characteristics can take him. The combination of individual skill, ball carrying, strength to compete physically and understanding of the game helps to explain why he can already produce against much older opponents.

Dowman was born on 31 December 2009 and joined Arsenal as a child. His progress through the youth ranks was so rapid that, at 13, he was already playing for the Under-18s. In September 2024, aged 14 years and eight months, he made his debut in the UEFA Youth League, an Under-19 competition, and became the youngest scorer in the history of the tournament.

The midfielder began training with the first team at 14 and took part in the 2025 pre-season. In August of that year, aged 15 years and 235 days, he made his Premier League debut against Leeds United. He was the second-youngest player to appear in the competition’s history, behind only Ethan Nwaneri, his Arsenal team-mate.

In November 2025, an even more significant milestone arrived. Coming on in the 3-0 win over Slavia Prague in the Champions League, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the tournament’s history, aged 15 years and 308 days. He was also the first 15-year-old to play in the competition.

The 2025-26 season brought two more high-profile records. In March, he scored against Everton and, aged 16 years and 73 days, became the youngest scorer in Premier League history, beating James Vaughan’s mark by 197 days.

Months later, he went down in Arsenal history as the youngest player to win the Premier League. The medal came at 16 years and 144 days, when the club ended a 22-year wait for the title. In October, he received three Guinness World Records certificates for the achievements.

Now, the England Under-21s have added two more chapters. Dowman made his debut for the side against Portugal on 13 November, aged 16 years and 317 days, surpassing Bellingham’s mark as the youngest player to represent the age group. On the following Monday, he started for the first time and scored the winning goal against France, aged 16 years and 320 days. Bellingham had scored his first Under-21 goal aged 17 years and 67 days.

Records broken for Arsenal and England (born 31/12/2009)

If he scores for the senior England team before 12/11/2027, Dowman will surpass Wayne Rooney (17 years and 317 days, in 2003) as the youngest scorer for England.

Age in years (y) and days (d) on the date of each record. n/a = previous holder not confirmed by an official source. Data up to 17/11/2026.

Sources: Arsenal, Premier League, ESPN and TNT Sports

Dowman’s main characteristic is his ability to carry the ball and beat opponents. He finds it easy to receive under pressure, shield possession with his body and change direction in tight spaces. He does not rely on straight-line speed alone: he uses feints, changes of pace and short movements to unbalance defenders.

Dowman already had a physique that allowed him to compete with older players, but he has also developed an intelligent way of using his body to protect the ball. That explains why he does not seem so intimidated when facing professional defenders.

Left-footed, he usually plays on the right, from where he can cut inside and use his dominant foot. The position also allows him to receive wide, draw the opposing full-back and choose between accelerating towards the box, combining with a team-mate or finding a pass inside. His ball control and ability to change the direction of play make him a particularly difficult threat to handle one-on-one.

But reducing him to a dribbling winger would ignore an important part of his repertoire. Dowman also has experience playing as an attacking midfielder and in deeper roles. In the youth ranks, he even played as a deep-lying midfielder. This variety helped him develop a broader understanding of space and the different roles on the pitch.

That versatility is an advantage for Arteta. At Arsenal, Dowman has already been used on the right and in central positions. When he receives between the lines, he can turn quickly and carry the ball towards the opposition defence. If he starts wide, he can attack the space between full-back and centre-back, moving closer to the box to shoot or take part in a combination.

There are also signs that his play without the ball matches his technical quality. In the win over France, Lee Carsley highlighted the teenager’s defensive performance, as he dropped back to intercept a pass and joined the pressing of opponents. A willingness to recover, press and take part in collective actions is an important requirement for earning a place in a side like Arteta’s.

Dowman’s rise inevitably prompts comparisons. His path recalls, in some respects, that of Nwaneri, who also made his Arsenal debut very young and had to find space in a competitive squad. Both came through the youth ranks playing in central positions, but had their first opportunities in the first team on the right.

The difference is that Dowman seems to have an even clearer ability to carry the ball at speed and beat opponents one-on-one. That does not mean it is possible to determine who will have the more successful career.

Arsenal also have reason to manage expectations. The recent episode against Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup highlighted one area of concern. After suffering a heavy challenge, the teenager reacted and was sent off, receiving a three-match ban. Arteta criticised the player publicly and said professional football is not an environment protected from provocation and the consequences of one’s own actions.

There is also the question of workload. A player who starts playing professional matches so early needs physical and emotional support. Arsenal have recent experience of integrating young players such as Saka, Nwaneri and Lewis-Skelly, but each athlete has his own process.

His first professional contract will be signed when he turns 17 on 31 December, after he agreed a pre-contract with Arsenal in January. The decision to stay at the club is important for the continuity of a development that has been closely monitored since the youth ranks.

The path to the senior England team is also open, but does not need to be taken immediately. Bellingham, who lost the Under-21 records to Dowman, played only four matches at that level before being promoted to the senior team.

For now, the best way to assess Dowman is to look at what he can already do, without turning every record into a career prediction. The rest depends on development, opportunities and careful management.

#1595. Chelsea’s £43m Winger Gamble Is Stalling: Should They Accept A Discount?

Chelsea transfer news: Birmingham Live reports that Alejandro Garnacho’s future needs resolving, because the winger has not started a match for Aston Villa and a permanent move depends on certain conditions being met. Chelsea sent the 22-year-old to Villa Park on a season-long loan in July, with a reported £43m obligation to buy next summer. Neither club has revealed the trigger, and reports link it to appearances.

The numbers explain the concern. FotMob lists four Premier League outings, all from the bench, without a goal or assist, while Football365 counts only 95 minutes across seven substitute appearances. Football Insider claims Villa are prepared to back out of the deal if his form doesn’t improve.

Garnacho’s strengths haven’t changed. His pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders earned a £40m move from Manchester United in 2025. The weakness is end product, and it followed him to London with eight goals in 43 games for Chelsea, only one of them in 24 Premier League appearances. Unai Emery left him out of the squad for the Manchester United game.

Chelsea have no obvious use for him either. Xabi Alonso told him in July that regular football wasn’t guaranteed, and the 3-4-2-1 Alonso favours uses Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer behind João Pedro, with Pedro Neto and Estêvão competing for the wide roles.

FotMob values him at about €29m (roughly £25m), far below the €71m peak recorded in August 2024, and Manchester United are reportedly entitled to 10 per cent of any future fee. If the clause isn’t triggered, he returns in July 2027 on a contract running to 2032.

Yes, and soon. Chelsea built the deal to protect £43m, but the clause relies on appearances from a manager who isn’t picking him, so the price drops with every unused substitution. The sporting case for a return is thin. Alonso’s system asks wide players to defend as wing-backs, while Garnacho’s value lies in isolating a full-back, and the £117m Rogers signing already covers the left-sided attacking role.

A mid-£20m sale, even after United’s cut, would still return more than half of the £40m Chelsea paid and clear a contract running to 2032. Chelsea should open talks with Villa in January about a lower fixed fee, or line up other buyers for the summer. A clause that depends on a manager picking a player he has benched was never a safe way to protect £43m.

#1591. Arsenal star Max Dowman smashes Jude Bellingham's record - but a less-familiar name should catch Thomas Tuchel's eye ahead of Euro 2028: THINGS WE LEARNED from England U21's defeat to Portugal

Published: 16:46 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 18:41 EST, 13 November 2026

Max Dowman smashed Jude Bellingham's record on an icy cold night in Bristol to become the youngest player to ever play for England's Under-21s.

The 16-year-old was sent on with 30 minutes to go by Lee Carsley in a move that energised an Ashton Gate crowd that went home frustrated after a 1-0 defeat inflicted by Afonso Moreira's first half goal.

But this was to be Dowman's night, smashing the previous record set by Bellingham when he made his England Under-21 debut against Kosovo in 2020 aged 17 years, two months and six days old. Dowman does not turn 17 until December 31.

Under-21s boss Lee Carsley has been keen long before this international break to try to shield Dowman from the weight of expectation.

But on he came, replacing the lively Amario Cozier-Duberry with a smile on his face and a quiet confidence that he didn't take long to show off, bursting past two Portuguese markers before four huddled together to gang up on him.

Breaking records is nothing new to a player that already holds one for being the Premier League's youngest-ever goalscorer, thanks to his goal against Everton last season.

Max Dowman wrote his name into the record books once more, playing for England Under-21s

Dowman came on to rich applause on a cold night in Bristol to shatter Jude Bellingham's record

The Arsenal teenager was lively playing off the right as he now targets the 2027 U21 Euros

Dowman is both the youngest player to ever win the Premier League and his outing in the Champions League against Slavia Prague last season saw the then-15-year-old become the youngest-ever player to appear in that competition.

By the time next summer's European Championships, which England will attempt to win for a third successive time, rolls around, rising star Dowman could well have earned the right to be this team's main man.

'We've only got three games left before the Euros [next summer],' Carsley explained.

'So it's important that he puts himself in the shop window to be on the plane.

'It's important that he keeps playing well, getting minutes, showing a really good attitude, like he has done.

'I thought he was outstanding when he came on tonight. I thought all of the subs made a real impact.

'I thought Max was unlucky not to get an assist... he made a great pass to Mikey Moore.

'He took up some really good positions, both in the 10 and out wide, he's got a big future ahead.'

His immense talent was one reason why Arsenal sent Ethan Nwaneri, who Dowman played alongside for part of his cameo, to Marseille on loan, and then similarly to Borussia Dortmund, eager not to block the 16-year-old's pathway.

Carsley knows the diamond he has on his hands and will want to take great care in helping polish a player that this crowd, this England team and this management group know has genuine world class potential.

Speaking of Nwaneri, this felt like a big camp for him. A big camp in the sense that he's falling down the pecking order at Dortmund and is back with a manager that has been so vital in his development.

Nwaneri was part of that 2025 group that won the Euros in front of Thomas Tuchel and he'll have seen the likes of Elliot Anderson and Alex Scott kick on to get to the seniors.

As previously mentioned, Nwaneri was moved out of the way by Arsenal to aid Dowman's development, not an easy pill for a player as talented as he is to stomach when his own development journey is at such a critical juncture given he is, to the surprise of many, still only 19.

'I think we have to remember his age as well,' Carsley added when asked about Nwaneri by Daily Mail Sport.

'He's very young is Ethan and he's another one that we've got a lot of hope for. He's got a lot of potential.'

Ethan Nwaneri was pushed to the side at Arsenal to benefit Dowman but England is different

Lee Carsley has been a crucial figure in the development of Nwaneri and this camp was timely

It was telling that even when Dowman came on, even with the groundswell of excitement at his introduction, it was Carsley's call to keep Nwaneri in his preferred No 10 position with Dowman slotting in on the right.

Nwaneri has only started four games on loan at Dortmund this season and has not managed a single start in the Champions League.

His close control, his quick burst over five yards and the fluidity of his movement was a timely reminder that yes, Dowman is the rising star everyone came out to see, but Nwaneri won't get pushed to the side again without a fight.

Amario Cozier-Duberry is a name not all will be familiar with but come next summer, with the Euros in his sights and promotion to the Premier League on the agenda with Middlesbrough, that could all be about to change.

The 21-year-old has had to be very patient, waiting until last month to make his debut at this level after years of finding himself overlooked.

Here, in what was just his third Under-21 appearance, he showed over the course of 61 minutes why the days of being looked past should be over.

One of the big frustrations in the FA right now at Under-21 level is the lack of touchline wingers. Rio Ngumoha, still only 18, has never been capped at the level and has instead been catapulted into the first team, while many, like Ethan Nwaneri, prefer playing inside.

'The more we can get our wide players one v one the better,' Carsley said. 'I think sometimes we leave them isolated and the opposition are able to double up on them.

Amario Cozier-Duberry is not a household name at international level but his talent is immense

'It's important that our game plan can't just be to get the ball wide and hope for the best.'

Dowman, on in place of Cozier-Duberry is a 10, rather than a right winger which is where he came on, and so a player like Cozier-Duberry, who is on loan at Middlesbrough from Brighton & Hove Albion, is worth his weight in gold.

Here in Bristol he was routinely drawing two defenders and at times three; Portugal knew full well how a quick flip-flap of the ball, or one clipped pass over the top, was enough for the Englishman to take the top off the back-line.

His loan at Bolton Wanderers last season complicated an international journey that has seen him play at Under-16, Under-17, Under-18, Under-19 and Under-20 level, but that's all in the past.

England need a genuine, pacy threat out wide if they are to win a third straight Euros. Cozier-Duberry showed here exactly why he should be it.

#1588. Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn

At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x

As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a new contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

“A joy to have him,” said Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

“Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta says Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z

Dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” said Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”

Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

It was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.

Arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

Given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

The only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub

On managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta said: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady says Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf

Asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta said: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”

He added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta said: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

“Individually some big performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”

Ipswich's first act of this game was to launch a long ball towards Marli Salmon and Zian Flemming. Salmon won the header, and then continued to win the overall battle with Flemming. Such an impressive performance by the 17yo. You don't see many defenders doing that at this age.

A post-match message to the support from Noni 🤳 pic.twitter.com/Eh6ojSkIfb

Arteta’s side are through to the fourth round of the League Cup.

Plenty of talking points: Dowman, Salmon and an ominous Arsenal showing... Leave your thoughts on the match and join the conversation in the comments section beneath this live blog.

Ipswich Town 2 Arsenal 4 (Akpom) Davis picks out Akpom who swivels to deceive Konsa before sweeping home. There was perhaps a foul in the build-up as Lewis-Skelly appeared to get held back by the goalscorer as he scrambled to get back.

There will be two minutes of time added on.

Dowman seemingly makes history with every touch of the ball. A remarkable talent.

16 - The three youngest players to score in the League Cup for a Premier League side all did so for Arsenal:16y 212d - Cesc Fàbregas (vs Wolves, 2003)16y 258d - Max Dowman (vs Ipswich, 2026)16y 266d - Jack Wilshere (vs Sheffield United, 2008)Production. pic.twitter.com/cKPqcFUrpP

16 - Max Dowman is just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side in all competitions, after Wayne Rooney in October 2002 for Everton against Wrexham, also in the League Cup.Generations. pic.twitter.com/75XN6hgGeS

Arsenal are finishing this match with a 16-year-old, 17-year-old and two 18-year-olds on the pitch. A good evening for the academy.

And right on cue, Salmon picks up the ball on the halfway line and drives forward, eventually forcing a foul from Nunez who goes into the book for his troubles.

Gyokeres finally gets a sniff at goal but Greaves is wise to his movement in behind and times a slide-tackle perfectly to poke the ball off for a corner.

Ibrahim comes on for Zubimendi before it is taken and joins the crew congregated at the far post but Walton punches Odegaard’s delivery away.

A really assured performance from Salmon, who has completed all 61 one of his passes and marshalled Flemming and Akpom with maturity beyond his years.

Chance! A high regain puts Mehmeti into a promising position in the right half-space, but his cross in to Akpom comes to nothing.

Tzolis, who is booed by the home fans owing to his Norwich connections, has a glimpse at goal but is immediately closed down before Ipswich earn a corner after a swift transition but it is easily dealt with.

There is an appeal for a handball off an Arsenal defender in the second phase of the set-piece but Egeli is offside so it matters not.

Just the 13 touches for Gyokeres tonight, make of that what you will...

Arteta shuffles the pack again, taking off Eze and Madueke for Tzolis and Odegaard.

Florentino tries his luck from the edge of the box, but his effort is comfortably saved by Kepa despite taking a slight deflection off Konsa’s Achilles.

It has been a relatively quiet night for Eze as Arsenal have prioritised attacks down the right. He twists this way and that and escapes the clutches of Furlong but his eventual effort sails well over.

Davis gets his teeth into the action right away. He swings in a cross from the left but it’s smothered by Kepa.

Ipswich’s substitutes have breathed some life into their attack. Akpom fires a cross-cum-shot towards goal but strikes the side-netting.

Another couple of substitutions for O’Neil, who will now be thinking about Everton next weekend. Davis and Walle Egeli are on for Ouattara and McAteer.

For those who are into your statistics, another Dowman goal here would create some history...

The record for the youngest hat-trick scorer across all professional tiers of English football belongs to Trevor Francis.

Playing for Birmingham City against Bolton Wanderers in Division Two on February 20, 1971, Francis scored four goals in a 4-0 win at just 16 years and 307 days old.

Guimaraes makes way for 18-year-old Julienne.

Ipswich Town 1 Arsenal 4 (Mehmeti) Clarke makes an immediate impact, bursting down the left before cutting the ball back to Mehmeti who had just held his run and is able to beat Kepa from 10 yards out.

Ipswich have been outgunned in the centre of the park, with Arsenal seemingly always creating plus-one and even plus-two situations.

O’Neil makes a pair of changes, replacing Philogene and Flemming with Clarke and former Arsenal striker Akpom.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 4 (Merino) Arsenal work the ball infield from the right in instalments, Madueke feeding Zubimendi who passes through Dowman to Merino on the edge of the box who opens up his body before guiding the ball around Walton.

Arsenal are FLYING!Merino puts another goal away for the Gunners 🔥 pic.twitter.com/nrzHHk1bou

Max Dowman was first spotted by Arsenal at four years old. He’s been running past opponents and scoring goals ever since. Now he’s just doing it on the professional stage, in front of the watching world, but it still looks completely normal to him.

Chance! It could, and maybe should, have been four. Merino threads a wonderful through-ball beyond Ipswich’s final line of defence and Madueke steals in to poke the ball across the face of goal with the outside of his left boot. Gyokeres was in the middle but could not divert the ball goalwards.

Kepa stretches to claim a looped Flemming cross which had echoes of the Spaniard’s game-defining error in last year’s League Cup final. This time he collects with a minimum of fuss. That Flemming was so far out on the left will be of concern to O’Neil.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 3 (Dowman) Madueke picks out Zubimendi in the box who in turn finds Dowman in the right half space and he gallops on to the ball before arrowing the ball past Walton. The assist had grazed Greaves’ outstretched arm and would surely have led to a penalty had Dowman not done the honours.

Max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x

Arsenal’s kick-off routines caused a stir last season, but this term they have mixed things up once more. Here, Zubimendi lays off Lewis-Skelly, who punches in a line-breaking pass to get Arsenal on the front foot from the off.

Zubimendi gets us going again for the second 45 minutes. Konsa has replaced Gabriel at the interval.

Such is the midfielder’s versatility, his heat map tonight paints a wildly different picture to that from his 45 minutes at the Stadium of Light over the weekend. He has played the midfield-sentry role in Suffolk and has executed it well.

It is further evidence as to why Arteta was hell bent on signing him in the summer. You would imagine his all-conquering presence will relieve pressure from Rice and Zubimendi’s shoulders. They were out on their feet by the end of the last campaign.

Arteta’s nine changes are looking fairly sensible now. He will be particularly pleased to have seen fringe players like Dowman and Madueke get on the scoresheet so emphatically. Arsenal will need their full squad to achieve their lofty goals this season and that half will give Arteta confidence that they have enough firepower to last the course.

We’ll play one minute of time added on...

Arsenal inject a bit of calm to proceedings with a healthy spell of possession. Their horizontal and vertical rotations (Lewis-Skelly is now minding to drop into that Rice role alongside the centre-backs) are proving tricky for Ipswich to track.

Gyokeres gets a shot away after a clever run in behind by Merino but cannot get enough pace behind his strike to trouble Walton.

Mehmeti brings down a searching ball from deep and faces up to Gabriel as he enters Arsenal box. Such is the Brazilian’s poise, though, that even when the Ipswich forward appears to have worked a yard of space, he telescopes in his leg and stops Mehmeti’s advances with perfunctory ease.

Ipswich are getting more bodies forward, with both full-backs bombing on. The ball is worked out to Furlong out on the right but, in a promising position, he loses his footing and the ball rolls out of play.

Next comes a foray down the left, Philogene beats Salmon on the outside but Kepa gets down smartly to cut out his cross. The next goal will naturally go a long way to determining how this tie plays out.

Ipswich are in the ascendancy and Greaves heads goalwards off a corner but does not get the requisite contact to beat Kepa. Arsenal launch a swift counter which is snuffed out by McAteer, illegally, and he goes into the book.

Ipswich might have thrown the towel in at 2-0 but they are pushing quite hard here and have caused Arsenal a few problems since the second goal. Philogene looks particularly dangerous on the left flank.

Outtara has been Ipswich’s best attacking outlet and he threads another lovely ball into the path of Philogene who is just beaten to it by Gabriel. The subsequent corner is punched away by Kepa.

Kepa goes long and Greaves misjudges the flight of the ball. Madueke looks to be in, but Ipswich’s centre-half recovers well and is able to block the eventual effort.

Merino picks out Dowman between the lines and the teenager is straight into Ipswich’s backline. His effort is well-struck but is charged down and cleared to safety.

Better from Ipswich! Their best shot at getting back into this contest is through counters when Arsenal are not set, and here Outtara bursts down the left before swinging in a deep cross to Flemming who cuts the ball back to Mehmeti who fires the ball just over the crossbar.

Guimaraes is slotting in between Arsenal’s split centre-backs in Arsenal’s build-up and Ipswich are not prepared to go three vs three that high up the pitch meaning the Brazilian has all the time in the world to dictate play from there. We’ve seen this all season long from Rice.

Arsenal are in complete control. Madueke flashes a delivery across the face of goal which is just cut out by Kipre before Gyokeres can get a foot in.

Arsenal’s midfield is so powerful and they showed it there, as Guimaraes slammed into one tackle and then Merino followed up with another to create the chance for Madueke. Arsenal are completely dominant here.

A flurry of chances for Ipswich. Philogene’s lopping cross is tipped away by Kepa but the ball falls to Flemming at the back post and his effort pinballs around a thicket of Arsenal limbs before reaching Florentino on the edge of the box, whose effort sails over the bar.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 2 (Madueke) That is goal of Ipswich’s own making. Walton’s loose pass out is picked off by livewire Guimaraes, and Merino spins in a ball in behind for Madueke to stride on to and spear beyond Walton into the bottom corner.

Arsenal are flying 🔥Noni Madueke adds a second for the Gunners 🔴 pic.twitter.com/gAVmAI3odx

Florentino’s loose pass is picked off by Dowman and the youngster earns a free-kick as the Ipswich midfielder attempts to recover. It’s taken quickly and Eze bursts into the box - there is a half-hearted shout for a penalty as the ball appears to strike Ouattara’s arm but the contact appears incidental and the referee waves play on.

Max Dowman’s second goal for Arsenal is quite similar to his first, scored so thrillingly against Everton last season. On both occasions he has put an opposition defender face-first in the turf before scoring the goal. Outrageous ability with the ball at his feet.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn

Ipswich earn a free-kick on the left by-line but Gyokeres does his job at the near post and heads away Nunez’s delivery.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 1 (Dowman) Simply majestic. A simple one-two with Eze on the left has Dowman running at Ipswich’s defence. He drops his shoulder and sells Kipre a dream before stroking the ball beyond Walton. “1-0 to the champions” sing the travelling fans.

Lewis-Skelly bursts down the left and picks out Dowman on the edge of the box. He attempts to tee up Guimaraes but Nunez gets a toe in and is able to avert the danger.

Early indications suggest Zubimendi will play in the nominal right-back position, inverting into midfield when Arsenal build up.

Madueke picks up the ball on the right flank and drifts inside before Guimaraes’ effort from the edge of the box is blocked.

Flemming gets us started. Ipswich kicking from right to left.

The players emerge from the Portman Road tunnel, Ipswich in their customary home blue shirts and white shorts, Arsenal in red and also white shorts. Last week Arsenal were made to change into red shorts to avoid a similar clash with Napoli, but apparently that’s no problem tonight. Modern football for ya!

Here’s a reminder of the line-ups in full:

Ipswich Town Walton; Furlong, Kipre, Greaves, Ouattara; Florentino, Nunez; McAteer, Mehmeti, Philogene; Flemming

Substitutes Palmer, Davis, O’Shea, Walle Egeli, Enciso, Clarke, Lukic, Maeda, Akpom

Arsenal Kepa; Zubimendi, Salmon, Gabriel, Lewis-Skelly; Guimarães, Merino; Dowman, Eze, Madueke; Gyokeres

Substitutes Meslier, Calafiori, Konsa, Tzolis, Odegaard, Ibrahim, Julienne, Saka, Havertz

Arsenal are warming up with Eze on the left, Madueke on the right and Dowman as the No 10 behind Gyokeres. In defence it looks like Zubimendi at right-back. The formation in the warm-up is not always the formation in the match, though...! They have played that trick before.

"You have to be patient with him" 🗣️Jamie Redknapp and Conor Coady on Max Dowman's potential for Arsenal 🙌 pic.twitter.com/O2bU0SQoJn

Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

Their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

It has meant that Gary O’Neil has had to leave established players out of match-day squads. “It was really tough leaving out Darnell [Furlong] and Anis [Mehmeti] from the squad [against Crystal Palace],” he said. “Doing that to good people is one of the toughest parts of the job. But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.

“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”

On Hincapie’s omission from the match-day squad:

“Some players were carrying some fatigue, some little issues that we have to look after and some other players are available, fresh and in better conditions to play.

On Timber being left out of tonight’s squad:

“Everything is fine, but obviously he has played much more than we would have wanted. He played 53 minutes [against Sunderland] after five months. I will need to look after him.”

When asked if Arsenal will set up with a back three tonight:

Alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies said Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”

The “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams said, everything else flows from there.

For much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

Tonight will be a good test for young Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who is the latest high-class graduate of the Arsenal academy. Arsenal have extremely high hopes for Salmon, who made four senior appearances last season. He could be in the centre of defence or at right-back tonight. I suspect Ipswich striker Zian Flemming might try to target Salmon with some physical challenges, especially in the air. Let’s see how he handles it.

Ipswich Town Walton; Furlong, Kipre, Greaves, Ouattara; Florentino, Nunez; McAteer, Mehmeti, Philogene; Flemming

Substitutes Palmer, Davis, O’Shea, Walle Egeli, Enciso, Clarke, Lukic, Maeda, Akpom

Substitutes Meslier, Calafiori, Konsa, Tzolis, Odegaard, Ibrahim, Julienne, Saka, Havertz

Max Dowman announced himself last season, showing off his gilded footwork in impressive cameos off the bench. Who could forget that lung-busting run and goal against Everton?

And while the 16-year-old winger featured in Arsenal’s pre-season, these will be his first minutes of senior football in the season proper. His only game time thus far has come in the Premier League 2 under-21s competition and he was not included in the match-day squad at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.

When asked about Dowman after the victory at Sunderland, Arteta said: “I wish we could have him here, but we have the limitation with the numbers that we can have. He will have his chance, he will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else. We know the talent that we have, we know the players that we have there and we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop and help the team.”

Although keeping Ipswich in the Premier League must be Gary O’Neil’s primary goal, he has insisted that the club will embrace opportunities in the cups.

When asked how he would approach tonight’s tie, O’Neil said: “We’ll have a strong side, we’ve worked our socks off in the transfer window to give ourselves a strong squad. Of course, a different level to Arsenal, but we’ll be strong on Tuesday and we’ll do our best to win the game.

“The club has worked so hard to have these moments and of course it’s a cup game, but to have Arsenal and Liverpool come to Portman Road a week or so apart is what everyone has worked so hard for in recent years, so we’re going to enjoy it, we’re going to have a right go and worst thing that can happen is we lose to Arsenal.”

Good evening from Portman Road, where it’s a gorgeous night for football. Ipswich have made 10 changes, which is an indication of where this competition sits in their list of priorities. Arsenal have made nine.

The Arsenal line-up is quite hard to decipher. It looks like it might be Martin Zubimendi at right-back or centre-back. I’ll keep an eye on the warm-ups and report back shortly.

Gary O’Neil wins the rotation battle, raising Arteta’s nine changes with 10 of his own. Greaves the only survivor from last weekend’s win at Selhurst Park.

Your Town tonight! ✊ pic.twitter.com/EEYjPFww4Y

Young defender Marli Salmon comes into the starting XI as Mikel Arteta makes nine changes to the team that started against Sunderland on Saturday.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Introducing your Carabao Cup Gunners starting XI ✨🤝 @deel

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. Mikel Arteta’s side have won all six of their matches so far this season, but travel to Portman Road fresh off an incident-filled win over Sunderland which thrust officiating back into the spotlight after Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty having been – in Arteta’s words – “judo-rolled” by Dan Ballard.

After the match, the Arsenal manager said: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

This season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin issue. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.

A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.

#1587. Carnevali calls Juventus situation ‘not acceptable’ as squad enters retreat before Napoli

Juventus will stay together in a training retreat at the JTC Continassa from Friday 30 October until Sunday's game against Napoli, after a blunt meeting between Giovanni Carnevali, the players and Luciano Spalletti. That home fixture is now widely seen as decisive for the coach's future and the direction of the season.

A direct meeting with chief executive Giovanni Carnevali has put the Juventus players and their coach under heavy pressure before Napoli’s visit.

The trigger was the loss in Genoa. Kingsley Ehizibue struck in the 12th minute, and Tommaso Baldanzi added a second in the 28th. Spalletti apologised to the supporters afterwards. He said his side had been beaten in every area. He added that they had to raise their physical level and fighting spirit.

The squad travelled back by train overnight. The players went to the Continassa the next morning. Management spoke to them there before training. Carnevali reminded them of their responsibilities to the owners, the club and the fans. He said the coaching staff still had the club’s trust, Adnkronos reported. He also asked for a strong and concrete reaction on the pitch. With the club’s agreement, Spalletti then chose to keep the players together at the training centre until kick-off.

Clubs rarely call this kind of retreat. It shows how serious the mood is at the Continassa. The message from the top is twofold. Public backing for the coaching staff comes paired with pressure for results. That places heavy weight on a single fixture.

Both sides have four wins, two draws and three defeats from nine games, Corriere dello Sport reported. Napoli sit seventh and Juventus eighth.

The gap lies in front of goal. Napoli have scored 17 times. Juventus have managed 11. Juventus have conceded only 10, however. Those figures are consistent with a side whose problems lie more in attack than in defence. A reaction against Napoli would need goals as well as fighting spirit.

Napoli will be without their coach. Massimiliano Allegri’s two-match ban covers their league games against Monza and Juventus. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea also fined him 10,000 euros. The sanction followed his abuse of match officials and later behaviour in the changing rooms during Napoli’s 3-3 draw with Roma. Napoli first announced an appeal. Allegri later said he had decided to drop it. That leaves Juventus facing a Napoli side without Allegri in charge at a moment when their own coach is under pressure.

The last meeting between the sides in Turin, on 25 January 2026, ended in a 3-0 Juventus win at the Allianz Stadium.

Juventus host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November 2026, with kick-off at 20:45.

#1586. Lots to work on but Pocognoli firmly believes Scotland ARE on the right track under his stewardship

Published: 18:44 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 19:02 EST, 13 November 2026

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli admitted his side were far from perfect in their Nations League win over North Macedonia – but he believes they ARE moving in the right direction under his stewardship.

The victory puts the Scots one point behind second-placed Slovenia in Group B1, ahead of Monday’s trip to runaway leaders Switzerland.

John McGinn notched a second-half double to secure a hard-earned second win of this campaign and Pocognoli’s first in front of the Hampden crowd.

‘We knew before the game that it [a win] will help to build a winning culture,’ he said. ‘And would make the work through the week end with a good feeling.

‘In terms of what we produced on the pitch, I know exactly what we worked on this week. I’m quite satisfied about what I see in some moments of the game, about the work on the ball and off the ball.

‘It was not always perfect but we created a lot of chances that we should score and maybe have a better feeling of the game.

Sebastien Pocognoli got his Hampden win as Scots boss after a 2-1 win over North Macedonia

Stalwarts John McGinn (left) and Andy Robertson applaud the Hampden crowd at full-time

‘Off the ball, I think we were quite aggressive. We recover a number of balls that we managed well in some moments of transition.

‘We created a big chance for Billy [Gilmour] from this also. So that’s a new approach of the game.

‘We created chances and we had a lot of pressure in the side of Macedonia. After the first goal I think we need to learn not to drop the intensity. Because after the first goal for five minutes I really feel like we dropped the intensity and the focus. So, it’s something that we need to fix.’

Asked whether his side need to be more clinical, Pocognoli added: ‘Yes, probably. But I prefer to talk about this with creating a lot of chances. We should score two or three. And probably we should have kept a clean sheet. So that’s really the critical aspect and the demanding aspect.

‘But it’s part of the challenge and we are early in the challenge to try to fix this for the future.’

Talisman McGinn put the Scots ahead on 54 minutes before Elmin Rastoder headed the visitors level against the run of play shortly after, with McGinn then stepping up to convert what turned out to be the winning penalty after a foul on Ben Gannon-Doak with 16 to play.

The Aston Villa midfielder has now taken his tally to 24 for the international team – just six behind legends Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law.

His manager is confident that it is only a matter of time before the 32-year-old is standing alone as his nation’s top scorer, and believes McGinn will have plenty of opportunities to smash the record playing in his team.

John McGinn scored from the penalty spot to clinch an unconvincing victory

He said: ‘I’m more focused on the collective challenge and goals. And I believe if we can build something nice around the collective, then John will one day break the record.

‘We created a lot of chances through these five [Nations League] games together. The individual record is important, but I always focus on the collective package.’

McGinn admitted that chasing the record is in the back of his mind and stressed his relief that he’s back among the goals after a lean spell at international level.

‘It’s been something that’s been in the back of my head, but obviously the results haven’t been the way we’ve wanted,’ said McGinn.

‘The team come first, but whether it’s myself, Scottie (McTominay), Che (Adams), anyone that’s going on the scoresheet at the minute, we’ll take it.

‘It’s been a bit of a dry patch for me over the past year or two on the goal front, so I’m delighted to get back on that trail and hopefully the same again Monday.

‘I feel good. I’ve still got many years to go, but the first priority is getting Scotland back to another major tournament and we’ll take it from there.’
